implied_side.book: captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings
implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 10.7 points toward North Texas of the quote EdgeDesk captured at captured consensus (stale) · 1 book · best at DraftKings. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 60.1 sat 2.1 points above the captured total of 58.

closing_line.why: no closing line is held for this game: the Collective captured none and the schedule feed carries none. Closing-line value is left blank rather than estimated from the result.

reasons: 1 of 1 gradeable claims held up and none was contradicted. The game was decided by the things EdgeDesk said would decide it.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — a 3-turnover swing — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a away margin of 9.2 and the game finished 1 the away way — 8.2 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: A 3-turnover swing
variance_markers.text: Tulsa Golden Hurricane won the turnover battle by 3. Turnover margin is the least repeatable thing in football: it moves scoreboards hard and predicts almost nothing about the next meeting, so a result built on it says less about either team than the scoreline suggests.

variance_markers.label: A 1-point game
variance_markers.text: A game this close is decided inside the noise of any projection. Whichever way it fell, it is weak evidence about either team.

verdict.line: The number landed and the reasoning behind it held up. That is the case EdgeDesk is trying to produce, and it is the only one of the four where the result is evidence the process works.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 8 of the claims in this article rested on model, passing, rushing, continuity.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver; the read does not name a side, so there is no direction to test.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for model, passing, rushing.

lessons.pregame_expectation: EdgeDesk published a fair total of 60.1.
lessons.actual_result: The game finished with 89 points, an error of 28.9.
lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.
